jobs.title: Processing Lab Technician
jobs.description:
Position Overview

The lab technician is responsible for maintaining processing tanks and the batch treatment area in compliance with applicable policies, procedures, and regulations. The lab tech uses lab equipment to prepare reagents and solutions, troubleshoot lab and test‑related problems, and review test results to ensure standards are met. Typical duties also include measuring levels, pH, and other chemical composition; coordinating and performing chemical adjustments and tank cleaning in accordance with safety procedures, internal work processes, and applicable regulations. This position is classified as safety‑sensitive.

This role is identified as requiring ITAR compliance; qualified candidates must meet the definition of a U.S. Person (per EAR Part 772 and ITAR 120.15):

• An individual who is granted U.S. citizenship

• An individual who is granted U.S. permanent residence (Green Card holder)

• An individual who is granted status as a "protected person"

Essential Functions

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made for qualified individuals with disabilities.

• Maintains processing tanks and batch treatment area per established procedures and regulatory standards; performs "Adds", "Decant", "Builds" and "Drops" of processing tanks as appropriate

• Prepares lab reagents/solutions

• Maintains and operates lab equipment, including pipettes, burettes, TDS, and pH meters; troubleshoots basic lab and test‑related issues; ensures proper use, care, and storage of equipment

• Performs "Adds", "Decant", "Builds" and "Drops" of processing tanks

• Completes accurate, timely, and legible quality records in accordance with AS9100 Quality Policy and NADCAP requirements; inputs QC data into the information management system

• Completes regulatory and hazardous waste reporting and disposal records as required

• Coordinates with internal/external sources for preventative maintenance schedules on all lab equipment

• Reviews customer specifications and identifies applicable data analysis requirements, pass/fail criteria, modulus calculations, test set‑up and configuration

• Maintains quality procedures, quality assurance instructions, and process control procedures to conform to all applicable customer requirements, industry standards, and registration systems; supports and participates as needed in AS/ISO/Nadcap/customer/supplier quality audits of process and products

• Assists in continuous improvement initiatives to enhance quality, productivity, and cost‑effectiveness based on observations and experience; provides technical expertise and works with operators to identify and implement improvements to reduce waste and improve efficiency; implements lean principles, techniques, and methods as appropriate

Work Experience

• Minimum of 1 year experience in a quality role in a manufacturing environment is required

• Previous experience in laboratory operations is required

• Comprehensive understanding of engineering drawings as it relates to the technical aspects of manufacturing and engineering is required; must be able to accurately read and interpret technical drawings and specifications

• Current/Recent HAZOPER and RCCRA certification preferred

Other Required Skills And Abilities

• Must pass a vision color test at pre‑employment and periodically thereafter

• Must be able to pass Hazwoper and RCCRA exams within a reasonable period after hire and must maintain certifications throughout employment in role

• Understanding manufacturing, material flow, process change, and quality processes is preferred

• Experience in continuous improvement concepts such as Six Sigma and Lean is preferred

• Knowledge of and experience with the requirements of AS9100

• Knowledge in RCCA (Root Cause Corrective Action) Analysis

Physical Demands and Work Environment

• Regularly stand and walk throughout the facility, stand for long

jobs.title: Electrical & Instrumentation Journeyman (Oil & Gas Manufacturing)
jobs.description:
Position Summary

We are seeking an experienced Electrical & Instrumentation Journeyman Level II to support the build, wiring, testing, and commissioning of oil & gas measurement equipment, including meter tubes, ultrasonic meter runs, orifice systems, sample systems, and packaged measurement skids. This role is ideal for a technician with strong electrical fundamentals and hands-on instrumentation experience who can work independently in a manufacturing environment.

Key Responsibilities
• Install, wire, and terminate electrical and instrumentation components for:
• * Ultrasonic, turbine, and orifice meter systems
• Flow computers, transmitters, and RTDs
• Sample systems, analyzers, and probe assemblies
• Control panels, junction boxes, and skid-mounted I&E systems
• Perform conduit routing, cable tray installation, cable pulls, and panel terminations according to shop standards.
• Read and interpret electrical schematics, loop sheets, wiring diagrams, P&IDs, and measurement drawings.
• Assist in the build and testing of measurement skids, including powering up systems, verifying signals, and supporting FAT procedures.
• Troubleshoot electrical and instrumentation issues using multimeters, loop calibrators, and diagnostic tools.
• Support measurement PM’s and drafting teams with redlines, revisions, and technical feedback.
• Document work performed, materials used, and test results for QA and traceability.

Required Qualifications
• Valid Journeyman Electrician License (state-issued).
• 2–3 years of electrical experience.
• Working knowledge of instrumentation, including transmitters, flow computers, RTDs, solenoids, and control wiring.
• Ability to read and interpret P&IDs, loop sheets, wiring diagrams, and measurement schematics.
• Proficiency with hand tools, power tools, and electrical test equipment.
• Ability to lift 50+ lbs, work in fabrication environments, and perform physically demanding tasks.
• Strong attention to detail and commitment to measurement accuracy.

Preferred Qualifications
• Experience working in fabrication, skid manufacturing, or with oil & gas equipment.
• Experience wiring PLC/VFD panels, motor controls, and low-voltage control systems.
• Knowledge of hazardous area classifications and wiring methods (Class I Div 1/2).
• Experience supporting FAT testing, signal verification, and commissioning.

About the Opportunity

The Scientific Programmer II bridges the gap between scientific development and operational production by integrating, testing, validating, and supporting scientific software applications in a remote work environment. This role collaborates with Science Teams, developers, and stakeholders to document requirements, establish test baselines, verify outputs, and ensure code changes are successfully transitioned into reliable operational environments.

Success is demonstrated through accurate integrations, effective stakeholder coordination, high-quality testing and documentation, and the delivery of dependable production-ready solutions.

The Scientific Programmer II supports the integration, testing, validation, and operational deployment of scientific software and algorithms, ensuring accurate, reliable, and production-ready solutions.

• Understand and document algorithm inputs, outputs, and production rules across all units, including how requirements differ between units, to ensure accurate implementation and operational consistency.

• Demo code and production rules at delivery, and provide ongoing guidance and support during transition to facilitate successful adoption and operational handoff.
